The direction of rates in the coming weeks is expected to shape the housing market's momentum next year, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association CEO Bob Broeksmit.

Meanwhile, the Federal Reserve governors are advocating a restrictive monetary policy stance to ensure that inflation returns to its 2% target. And, a downward pressure on economic activity is not expected to bode well for commercial real operators.
The S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) decreased 4.34% week-over-week to 270.54 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF
was down 4.30% to $42.46.
The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index dropped 3.95% on a weekly basis, while the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index fell 3.98%.
Weekly Winners & Losers
Data center REITs and telecom tower REITs led the weekly losers among largecap stocks as Wall Street's enthusiasm on technology and artificial intelligence fizzled out.

Data center projects face significant challenges, including power constraints and community opposition. Additional concerns include the potential adoption of cheaper open-weight AI models and high correlation among AI stocks, which could amplify volatility, according to a recent report by S&P Global Market Intelligence.
Iron Mountain
(-10.14% W/W to $102.22), Digital Realty Trust
(-9.74% W/W to $162.46), and Equinix
(-8.12% W/W to $968.22) were the notable decliners.
Crown Castle
and SBA Communications
pulled back by 9.28% and 8.46% to $82.40 and $173.33, respectively.

This week, Crown Castle said at the Morgan Stanley European Technology, Media, and Telecom Conference that the business is entering a transition year marked by softer near-term leasing trends and heavy cost work.
Lineage

topped the midcap losers, retreating 11.58% week-over-week to $31.22. The stock hit its 52-week low on Friday amid a broader technology and market rout, which began after the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
Rithm Capital
followed, with a 10.26% pull back to $8.05. The mortgage REIT stood out as a significant decliner as mortgage rates jumped, weighing on application activity.
Uniti Group
(-25.29% W/W to $1.95), and Real REMAX
